The Minnesota African American Family Preservation and Child Welfare Disproportionality Act requires active efforts and incorporation of the family's social and cultural values in case planning and reunification. changes.after:
DCYF's 2026 interim report analyzes child protection involvement in 2023. Using an African American/Black category that includes children identified as that race alone or with another race, the figures round to 17 percent of Minnesota's child population and 27 percent of children involved in child protection. Here, involvement means a child was named as an alleged victim in a screened-in maltreatment report with a completed assessment or investigation; each child was counted once. These figures describe disproportionate involvement, not a finding about any individual family.

The Minnesota African American Family Preservation and Child Welfare Disproportionality Act establishes active-efforts responsibilities and attention to family social and cultural values. Statewide implementation begins January 1, 2027. In 2026, the Legislature appropriated $15 million in one-time county funding for that implementation. Check current implementation guidance and the requirements that apply to the case with the policy owner.
